contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of how to generate own ideas for artistic expressions about the people based on their history and culture, the environment and topical local/national/global issues
indicatorDescription: Study some visual artworks created by Ghanaian and other African visual artists living in Africa and examine how the artworks reflect the history and culture of the people in Africa
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to: study some visual artworks created by Ghanaian and other African visual artists living in Africa and examine how the artworks reflect the history and culture of the people in Africa
competencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Communication and Collaboration; Creativity and Innovation; Personal Development and Leadership; Cultural Identity and Global Citizenship; Digital Literacy
resources: NaCCA approved textbook; TLMs; ICT tools; community resources
rpk: Learners sing, dance, draw, mould and role-play from Basic 1-4; they see Ghanaian artworks and performances at festivals, durbars and in the media.
starter: Greet learners with a creative warm-up clap / body percussion.
Show picture charts and real artworks linked to today's lesson; ask 'What can you see? How does it make you feel?'

NEW TODAY (Week 1): Creative Arts – we study some visual artworks created by Ghanaian and other African visual artists living in Africa and examine how the artworks reflect the history and culture of the people in Africa
Introduce tools/materials and safety rules for handling them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Demonstration – 5 min): Teacher models the skill using picture charts and real artworks – study some visual artworks created by Ghanaian and other African visual artists living in Africa and examine how the artworks reflect the history and culture of the people in Africa
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice – 5 min): Pupils practise in pairs/small groups; teacher moves round scaffolding technique and safe use of tools.
ACTIVITY 3 (Creative Making – 7 min): Pupils create a small individual piece on the lesson's theme (b5.1.1).
ACTIVITY 4 (Showcase – 3 min): Mini gallery walk / performance; peer appreciation with 'two stars and a wish'; teacher feedback on creativity and craftsmanship.
plenary: Clean-up song – pupils tidy tools and materials together.
Reflection questions: 'What did you enjoy? What was challenging? What will you try differently?'
Homework: finish or practise today's artwork/song/dance at home with family.
Preview next Visual/Performing Arts lesson.
assessment: Class exercises; oral questions; practical performance; SBA

NEW TODAY (Week 1): Creative Arts – we study some artworks created by Ghanaian and other African visual artists studied that reflect the physical and social environments of some African communities Learners are to

ACTIVITY 3 (Creative Making – 7 min): Pupils create a small individual piece on the lesson's theme (b5.1.2).
ACTIVITY 4 (Showcase – 3 min): Mini gallery walk / performance; peer appreciation with 'two stars and a wish'; teacher feedback on creativity and craftsmanship.
plenary: Clean-up song – pupils tidy tools and materials together.
Reflection questions: 'What did you enjoy? What was challenging? What will you try differently?'
Homework: finish or practise today's artwork/song/dance at home with family.
Preview next Visual/Performing Arts lesson.
assessment: Class exercises; oral questions; practical performance; SBA
